rationale: A wins because it mostly keeps its feet inside the fact pattern and names the holes before a reporter does. Its “Substack bets native video can answer the revenue question its funding struggles raised” is a defensible business angle if the funding history and revenue math are sourced. B has sharper shapes, but “$400 million in creator earnings is an inconvenient number for the subscription fatigue narrative” smuggles in an outside thesis, then pretends “widely published since 2022–2023” came in the brief. That is how a clever angle becomes a fact-checking chore.
gaps_in_A: “Substack completes its swap from email newsletter to all-in-video media app” overstates the update. Native video plus a feed does not prove a completed swap or an “all-in-video” strategy.
“short-form, algorithmic-style feed” adds mechanics the update does not provide. The brief says “TikTok-style feed,” not short-form ranking, algorithmic distribution, or open discovery.

“The numbers behind Substack's ‘struggling platform’ reputation don't add up” outruns the evidence. Creator earnings and paid subscriptions do not answer profitability, runway, valuation, or funding struggles without denominator and revenue context.
“move the needle” is cliché sludge in an otherwise disciplined set. Cut it; the business question is whether the 10% take rate produces meaningful revenue.
gaps_in_B: “widely published since 2022–2023” is an invented support beam. The subscription-fatigue narrative may be real, but it was not in the update and needs sourcing before it anchors an angle.

“implying $40M or more flowed to Substack from top creators alone” is useful but too confident. The brief does not say whether the $400M is gross revenue, net creator earnings, or how the 10% cut is calculated.
“creator-controlled audiences” imports Substack positioning that is not in the supplied facts. Fine as a hypothesis, sloppy as a stated contrast with YouTube and TikTok.
“a specific writer with 10,000 paid subscribers” invents a creator profile. Use the creator-operator angle, but keep the example generic until you have a real creator on record.
